subject: Translating messy business requirements, stakeholder language, and early product ideas into an implementation-neutral…

evals.prompt: Define conceptual-modeling in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the conceptual-modeling skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind conceptual-modeling. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "give me the physical table design with PKs, FKs, and normalization forms". Should conceptual-modeling activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force conceptual-modeling onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to taxonomy-design, data-modeling, entity-relationship-modeling, semantic-relations, ontology-modeling, bounded-context-mapping, naming-conventions, code-review.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "a stakeholder says users place orders that ship in multiple boxes -- how do I capture this as a model before naming tables?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying conceptual-modeling.

Place conceptual-modeling among its adjacent skills (taxonomy-design, data-modeling, entity-relationship-modeling, semantic-relations, ontology-modeling, bounded-context-mapping, naming-conventions, code-review). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about conceptual-modeling and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
